User_Story: As an admin, I want to register a customer with a support tier so that SLA targets reflect their plan.
As an admin, I want to register an agent with availability and a capacity limit so that routing can pick the right person.
Notes: Prisma domain. status AVAILABLE/BUSY/OFFLINE; openTicketCount guarded by maxCapacity (default 5).

User_Story: As an admin, I want adding an agent to provision their login with the AGENT role via an email invite so that they can start working tickets.
Notes: Provisioning. agent.create calls auth admin-create/invite with AGENT role (sync cross-service, getOutboundHeaders #24); stores userId. Apply sync-cross-service-call skill.

User_Story: As an admin, I want an Add agent modal capturing name, email, team and capacity so that I can onboard agents quickly.
Notes: Modal form; on submit creates agent + triggers the invite. data-testid: create-agent-form.

User_Story: As a customer, I want to raise a ticket with a subject, description and priority so that support can help me.
Notes: Prisma domain. Persist OPEN. slaDueAt derived from priority. comments relation. Actor from @CurrentUser (#23).

User_Story: As an agent, I want to list tickets filtered by status and priority so that I can work the queue.
As the system, I want assigning a ticket to synchronously verify the agent is AVAILABLE and under capacity before persisting so that I never overload an agent.
Notes: ACL — apply sync-cross-service-call skill. IAgentValidator validates status + capacity. getOutboundHeaders() (#24). Golden Rule #14.

User_Story: As the system, I want a new ticket to be auto-routed to an available agent asynchronously so that customers get a fast first response.
Notes: Saga step 1 — apply choreography-saga skill. ticket publishes TICKET_CREATED; agent-event-handler runs PickAvailableAgentUseCase (lowest load); replies TICKET_ASSIGNED | NO_AGENT_AVAILABLE. Idempotent.

User_Story: As an agent, I want a routed ticket to land in my queue or escalate when nobody is free so that nothing falls through the cracks.
Notes: Saga step 2. ticket-event-handler consumes TICKET_ASSIGNED/NO_AGENT_AVAILABLE; OPEN->ASSIGNED (set assignedAgentId) | ESCALATED. Replay = no-op.

User_Story: As a support lead, I want tickets that breach their SLA to be escalated automatically so that urgent issues surface.
Notes: SLA-breach timer publishes TICKET_SLA_BREACHED; handler transitions to ESCALATED. Idempotent.

User_Story: As an agent, I want a webapp ticket workspace with status badges and resolve/escalate actions so that I can work efficiently.
Notes: Client hooks in client-common. Action menu + status-variants.ts. data-testid: tickets-table.

User_Story: As a customer, I want a webapp portal to raise a ticket and track its status so that I can self-serve.
As an admin, I want a webapp agent roster showing load and availability so that I can balance the team.
